mentl/e5ae573:
The frontier against pin f862677e reads 368 pass / 10 red, and five of the
ten are one root that is neither the linking fix nor a bug in the collapse.
It is the deep-handler law, made true everywhere by the uniform bracket, and
the wheel not obeying it.

The backtrace is exact: ev_declaring_node <- format_one_stmt <-
op_format_default_format_program. format_program is an ARM of format_default,
and inside it format_one_stmt performs another Format op that format_default
itself declares. A deep handler is not installed for its own arms, so that
sibling perform walks past its own handler, finds no other Format install,
and hits the walk's refusal. Under the old lexical tier there was no bracket,
so it resolved to itself and worked. The wheel's handlers were authored
against the missing bracket.

The same root answers the escape fixture, which wanted exit 7 from a stateless
arm direct-called with no record after its install closed. Its own text calls
that the value-sound licence for stateless arms and reserves the choice for
band A. It is not a separate question: the bracket's content IS the install's
world, so an arm reached with no install has no world to run under. Making
the walk uniform answered it as a side effect, which means it now has to be
answered on purpose.

The form is a deletion, not a mechanism: an arm needing a sibling op already
has that op's implementation in scope, so performing it re-derives something
it holds. E_InitPerformsOwnOp already refuses the neighbouring case, and the
general shape should refuse at compile time rather than trap at runtime —
which also makes the restructure mechanical, since the diagnostic enumerates
the sites.

Stated plainly because it is the state: pin f862677e is not shippable. mentl
fmt and mentl space trap on real input. The micros stayed 149/0 the whole way
because they never run a verb whose handler arms perform sibling ops.
mentl/e5ce6e5:
The writer flip ran a third time, with the discriminator defect that
blocked it fixed, and the march came back CLEAN: m2 == m3, peak 2280480 KB
under a 2310000 ceiling. Two earlier attempts measured ~131.5k diff lines
with m4 trapping, and the record read that as the linked form breaking the
wheel. It was the five unannotated receivers the whole time. The semantics
are exonerated; PLAN and RESIDUE say so where they said the opposite.

The repin was still refused, and by the micro battery alone: 138 pass, one
fail, mn-findtag trapping at a marked "field offset unprovable" floor
reached from main. So the flip is not a self-hosting question. It is a
question about one micro's receiver.

Two eprints, one per writer, built into a probe m2 and run on the repro,
confirm what the record had inferred. On `fn pick(u: {zeta: Int, ...}) =
u.zeta` over `{alpha: 7, zeta: 9}` the open-open writer fires first with
both sides knowing one field and neither carrying an extra, so both close
to the empty residual; the call site's closed record then narrows a third
row var the body never reads. Under the flip that repro stops answering 7
and traps, which is the floor doing its job at the site it was built for.

mn-open-row-second-field runs findtag's exact flow but reads region_id,
the second-sorting field, where a layout over a partial set would land on
handle. The pinned boot answers 2. That shape is sound today and the flip
breaks it too, so it is the gate that catches this class before the march
instead of by it. Falsified two ways first: it fails against the flip
build and against a deliberately wrong expectation.

What stays open is narrower than the fork it replaces. findtag and the
zeta repro both close an empty residual and only one of them is wrong.
Why findtag's receiver resolves correctly through the same fabrication is
the next probe.

mentl/e5300a1:
parse_stmt splits into DISPATCH and MINT. parse_stmt_form returns a Stmt
per kind and never a span; parse_stmt stamps the extent once, from the
opening token it holds to the closing index it receives. Fn, let, type,
effect, handler, import and the bare-expression form all converted. The
four LetStmt mints that are DESUGAR sites -- nested fn, destructure
prepend-let -- keep their own spans, because they are not statements the
dispatcher opened.

Nineteen chances to remember an extent become one place that knows it.
FnStmt's span_join(start, body_span), correct only because someone
remembered, goes with the rest.

Two bugs surfaced on the way and both are closed. The closing index sits
one PAST the declaration and the predicate, variant and row paths all
return past a TNewline, so a naive join reached the next line and the
slice rendered a single character; span_last walks back over layout.
And source_slice destructured Span(sl, sc, _, ec), discarding the END
LINE and using ec as an offset into the START line -- so a multi-line
handler declaration rendered its closing brace's column as a
two-character fragment of its own keyword. Pre-existing, and invisible
for exactly as long as every declaration span was one token wide.

THE GATES CAUGHT TWO OF MINE. The quiet-gate ratchet refused authored
ref on the two new helpers (816 -> 817) and its message is the ruling:
teach the inference, do not annotate around it -- the markers came off
and the inference has them right. The comment-ref ratchet refused a
backticked two-character sample in my own prose, because a backticked
name is a claim.

Measured through the pre-pin wheel, every declaration slices its head
line and speaks its meaning: `type Colour = Red | Green : Colour -- 2
variant(s)`, `effect Tick { : effect Tick -- 1 op(s)`, `handler counter
with n = 0 { : handler counter -- 1 arm(s), 1 state field(s)`.

sonido/e530b73:
Introduces the single source of truth for a complete effect rig — graph
topology, per-node A/B parameter snapshots, six macro definitions, A/B morph
config, and globals — with three projections that all round-trip to the same
model: JSON (serde), a 4 KB binary QSPI sector, and the runtime engine.

New crate `sonido-patch` (no_std + alloc; `std` → serde/JSON):
  - Patch model: nodes (stable effect UID, not list position), edges with
    Input/Output/Split/Merge endpoints, MacroDef×6, MorphConfig, GlobalControls.
  - binary.rs: one hand-rolled codec compiled into both host (encode+decode)
    and firmware (decode only) — no second mirrored struct to drift, the bug
    that bit the legacy DaisyPresetSlot. "SNDP" magic, CRC32, fully
    bounds-checked decode that never panics on corrupt flash. Worst-case patch
    (8 nodes × 16 params A/B, 6 macros × 8 mappings) encodes to < 2 KB, well
    within one sector.
  - validate.rs: structural checks (always) + pedal-fit (effect set / CPU
    budget / SDRAM) taking cost tables as slices, so the crate never pulls in
    sonido-registry or the effect set and stays light enough for the firmware.
  - Tests: proptest binary+JSON roundtrips, CRC/truncation/bad-magic rejection,
    decode-never-panics on arbitrary bytes, worst-case-fits-sector. Builds and
    tests pass for thumbv7em-none-eabihf.

sonido-core: optional `serde` feature (no_std compatible) deriving on the small
shared POD enums; new MacroTarget/GlobalParam (macro_map) and MorphMode (morph)
that both the runtime MacroMap (Workstream B) and the persisted format share —
single source of truth, no parallel enums.

sonido-registry: append-only EFFECT_UIDS table + effect_uid/effect_by_uid, with
a totality+uniqueness test. UIDs are the permanent identity the wire format
stores; positional indices never leave a running process again.
clob/e562162:
Lays down the corpus-acquisition half of Phase L as a functional,
tested pipeline (no network or real run is triggered here -- those
stay user-initiated). The runtime path is wired and verified; the
download/first-run remain a deliberate manual step.

- clob encode (text -> .tokens) + src/token/tokens_file.rs: a trivial
  cache format (magic CLTK, version, count, u32xcount) kept separate
  from the .clob model format. load_tokens rejects bad magic, unknown
  version, truncated bodies, and trailing bytes -- a corrupt cache
  fails loudly rather than feeding garbage ids to the model.
- ingest consumes a .tokens cache when --input ends in .tokens,
  skipping BPE entirely; otherwise it tokenizes text as before.
  Verified byte-identical to text ingestion (295 episodes both ways).
- src/util/split_check.rs: sentence-level train/holdout contamination
  gate (ignores sub-5-word boilerplate). tests/data_split.rs enforces
  it and self-skips when no real corpus is present, so CI stays green
  on a fresh clone.
- scripts/acquire_corpus.sh + tokenize_corpus.sh: idempotent,
  checksum-pinned acquisition and tokenization. Default corpus is a
  public-domain Gutenberg text; PLAN's original example is in
  copyright and is not used.
- data/synthetic/{diagnostic.txt,expected.md}: a planted-pattern
  corpus (shift rule, periodic n-gram, period-2 alternation, noise
  control) documenting what the crystallization loop should find --
  the corpus-level analog of the Phase E synthesis test. Plus
  data/corpus/README.md provenance and .gitignore for derived files.

68 tests pass (cargo test --release). Still open for Phase L: the real
corpus run, a committed default tokenizer.bin, and the rolled-over
trajectory.rs / clob traj.
